neighbours.label: A person's stated readiness or intention to act in reported speech ('asked whether he would', 'said it would', 'ready to'), not habitual or conditional 'would/will'
fire: Reporters asked the governor whether she would veto the new tax bill.
The union said on Friday that it would strike if talks failed.
The striker told fans he was ready to fight for his place in the team.
When asked if he would run again, the mayor only smiled.
The opposition leader declared that she would not join the coalition.
The company insisted it was ready to cooperate with the investigators.
The prime minister was asked whether he would apologize for the remarks.
The rebels announced that they would lay down their arms by June.
quiet: As a child, she would spend every summer at her uncle's farm.
Water will boil faster if you put a lid on the pot.
The striker scored twice in the second half of the match.
On rainy days the mayor would read in the library downstairs.
The opposition leader spoke for an hour in parliament on Tuesday.
The company moved its headquarters to Denver last spring.
The old clock would chime loudly every hour through the night.
The rebels crossed the river at night and reached the town by June.

notes: Probe: 'asked whether he would resign' 0.94, 'ready to prove his innocence' 0.86, 'said it would launch' 0.41, 'announced the city will open' 0.17; habitual 'would often turn cold' 0.04, 'would walk to the market' 0.02, 'it will melt' 0.06.
